topics.topic: Clock-source capability ownership, wiring, and callers
questions: Which module owns the clock source, which capability exposes its wall and monotonic readings, and who creates and supplies it to identity operations, guards, use cases and the transport rate limiter?
Which named clock-source capability does the transport guard call for the viewer-entry rate-limit reading, and which component owns making exactly one such call per viewer-entry request?

Which named module capabilities provide the wall and monotonic readings, and which flow owner calls each capability for operation timestamps, expiry checks, audit timestamps and viewer-entry rate limiting?

quotes:
The source of time of A28: the only reader of the host wall clock and of the
host elapsed clock. One wall reading per call, the current UTC time as an
offset-naive datetime, and one elapsed reading per call, a monotonic count of
seconds as a float.

Each module's `Knows` section names exactly the modules it imports (the
accepted `imports.module_internal`, plus the one edge `api` → `api_irregular`
of the running code). Lines of the list are layers, not an
assertion that every module imports every earlier one.

- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
| A28 | `system_clock` | every module that reads the time (listed in `30_trace.json`) |
judgement.why: State 3 names `system_clock` as owner, names its wall and monotonic capabilities, defines `Knows` as direct importing, assigns every time-reading module as a consumer, and specifically assigns the elapsed call to `transport_guard`.

questions: What is the operation boundary for CLK-001: the whole request, each owning use case, or every independently called authentication/authorization capability?

judgement.why: P2 asks the same request-versus-operation wall-clock scope question on unchanged texts and already records the later operation-level resolution.

precedent.topic: Wall-clock read cardinality and scope within an HTTP request
quotes:
A28 (`occurred_at` from its own clock read at append, not the caller's
instant): exactly one insert; a service actor keeps its `key_version`; no secret or
`file_ref` enters the details.

append_audit: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

_authorize_project_operation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

set_section_progress: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
precedent.why: The later API and notes resolve “request” as each named operation taking its own single utc_now reading, with append_audit explicitly taking an independent reading rather than reusing its caller's instant.

questions: Which named capability obtains and projects the visible photos for the overview, and which module owns that operation?

topics.topic: Per-component failure classification in project overviews
questions: For each budget, expense, progress, payment and photo component, which failure classes become `temporarily_unavailable`, and which still propagate through `error_policy`?

quotes:
The project part turns a `RegistryBoundaryError` into
`temporarily_unavailable`; any other failure of the Registry context request
propagates. Each portal part (budget, expenses, progress, payments, photos)
turns `ScopedNotFoundError` into `not_configured` and every other failure of
its builder, an unexpected one included, into `temporarily_unavailable`, so
the overview itself then still succeeds.
judgement.why: The later public API explicitly classifies the project failure separately and specifies the outcome of every failure from each of the five portal-part builders.

topics.topic: Semantics of missing section progress records
questions: When a section has no progress record, is its `completed_work_value` `None` or zero?

quotes:
- Completed work value: `work_planned × completion_percent / 100`, rounded
  half-up to 2 digits per section, summed after rounding. A section without
  a progress record has no completed work value (`None`, never 0) and is
  left out of the sum, as it is left out of overall progress.

The completed work value of a section without a progress record is `None`,
not 0 (owner 2026-11-08: "«Нет данных» не должно выглядеть как ноль" —
missing data must not look like zero). This replaces the reading accepted
with the running service on 2026-11-06, where that value was `Decimal` 0
while its percent was `None`; the two now both say "not recorded". State 1
`BudgetSectionView` and `ProgressSectionView` type it `Decimal | None`. The
running service still returns 0 until the next Route B regenerates
`derived_views` (`spec/HANDOFF.md`).
judgement.why: State 2 makes `None` the normative result and expressly identifies zero as the superseded service reading, so the historical carried-change note does not prescribe a competing current outcome.
